data.translation: Am Morgen steht der König auf: Hallo! Da liegen seine sieben Feinde tot auf dem Dache, man hat die Schatzkammer ausgeraubt, der die bist gefesselt,

rationale: New ko-Preterit box, provisional morphological analysis; preserve the edition's textual irregularity.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.8/303)

data.turoyo: manhəbiwo as sale du muklo, du laḥmo, mahzəmiwo u laḥmo mu kafnaṯṯe.
data.translation: They would plunder the baskets of food, of bread; they would carry off the bread because of that hunger.

rationale: New Infectum-wa box; repeated plundering with overt baskets as patient.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.26/4435)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Koṯe l bolox i naqqa d qṭəlwo u ṣalḥoya wo... malwašwolən ǧule d ʕaskar, azzən li qəžla lašan d manhəbiwola, lašan d saymiwo mede we, lə koṯe l bolox Abuna?
data.translation: Jan: Do you remember the time when that man from Salah had been killed... they had put soldiers' clothes on them, they went to the barracks to plunder it, to do something, do you not remember, Father?

rationale: New box, distinct past purpose with incorporated feminine barracks object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 19/5)

data.turoyo: Qayəm ʕmile aʕma l Ḥamzo. Mšayaʕle l Diyab tre b lalyo, omər: “Zoxu qṭalulle. Kan lə ḥzalxu, anhebulle.”
data.translation: Da schickte Dijâb zwei in der Nacht, sie sollten den Ḥamzo ermorden; wenn sie ihn aber nicht fänden, sollten sie ihm seinen Laden ausplündern.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell; full conditional instruction is more informative than the inherited isolated anhebul-le.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; explicit first-person affected possessor.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (96/96)

data.turoyo: Kḥoyər: kale kito ḥarami, manhable i xazne du ḥakəm.
data.translation: Da sah er einen Dieb, der das Schatzhaus des Königs ausgeraubt hatte.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (96/118)

data.turoyo: u ḥaramiyano, maṣərre, manbahle i xazinayḏi
data.translation: Diesen Dieb, der mein Schatzhaus geplündert hat, hat man gefesselt.

rationale: Unusual repeated manbah- consonant order; source spelling retained explicitly rather than normalized.

summary: Direct nominal place/property patients alternate with suffix-coded affected people. PrS 59/74 has an l-marked interrogative agent and a first-plural affected group; 70/55 has a reciprocal object.
PrS 51/17 uses k-Infectum in distributive past narration; PrS 51/18 summarizes with Preterit. A past German translation alone cannot determine the box.

96/104 gmanhabbe is provisionally ko-Preterit: completed robbery is discovered and i xaznayḏe is singular feminine, favoring plural-agent Preterit manhabbe over a suffix-bearing Infectum with plural patient.
manbahle/manbahhe recur at 96/118, 191, 192 in unambiguous robbery contexts. The nhb/nbh order issue remains a source/dialect question; no token has been silently corrected or moved to 'notice'.
The root is identified as an Arabic borrowing in the inherited headword and takes Turoyo III morphology. This is a lexical verb, not evidence of a light-verb collocation.
Hors 3/30 is already cited as RT 30; 63/322, 29/91 and 71/21 are also existing examples. Their wording is not duplicated.
No new sense. Preterit and Infectum are already at least five after round 1, so stale reader thin-cell counts are not followed. Jan adds two contexts for the previously absent Infectum-wa box.
manhəbiwo has plural Infectum ending plus -wo; manhəbiwola adds a feminine patient after -wo and occurs under lašan d-. Past purpose/intention does not entail that the plundering happened.
Zero nominal patients alternate with incorporated -nne and -la. The 1.8/342 suffix may resume hidden possessions or tombs; do not force one referent.
The modern accounts retain the same lexical III plundering verb as round 1; no light-verb collocation or new contact etymology follows.
Confirm ko-Preterit gmanhabbe in 96/104 versus a contracted Infectum; the singular treasury patient supports the former.
Are repeated manbah- spellings in Ritter 96 metathesis, transcription error or another dialectal form? Confirm before altering consonant order.
Confirm the agent/patient segmentation of manhabballi (PrS 19/8), manhebile (19/14), and manhəbile (50/31).
At 1.8/342 does -nne in manhəbənne resume possessions, tombs or their owners?
Does lašan d manhəbiwola at 2.26/4435 mark an earlier plan, a narrative purpose or another temporal reading? Keep it in Infectum-wa from its morphology.
Restore the missing article in “to the poor”.
rationale: Here poor denotes a group of people and requires the article the. The Turoyo has the definite plural af=faqire. This is a missing word in the English translation.

summary: Patients may be a person/affected household, a shop, treasury, village or country. Animal societies in fables retain the same plundering event; these are participant extensions, not new senses.
Baskets of bread, vegetable plots, depot, bathhouse, barracks and city are patients or affected places within plundering; they do not establish food-taking or military-raid senses.
